text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.23% today to $137.35, continuing a six-day climb that has added 6% to the stock over two weeks. The driver is the sharp move in oil prices: crude has held above $97 domestically and $109 globally, well above the $100 level it had tested just days earlier. This strength reflects competing pressures — Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was shut down after drone attacks from Iran-allied Houthi militants, tightening supply, while hopes for Middle East peace talks (urged by China and India this week) offered some counterweight.

The stock's gain sits in a narrow band where geopolitical risk and negotiation signals are wrestling for control of the oil market. As long as crude stays elevated and supply disruptions persist, energy producers like ConocoPhillips benefit from wider profit margins, even as any breakthrough in peace talks could reverse that advantage just as quickly.
